column1: # DARWIN LINK-NAME ORACLE — what a REAL platform compiler emits for each C
# identifier the shipped descriptors import on Mach-O, per arch.
# every Mach-O-visible imported function in `src/dss-config/shippedLibs/**` to
# have a row here AND to declare the `linkName` this row implies. A symbol added
# to a descriptor without a row here goes RED — which is the whole point: the
# fixed table in `test_shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp` pins the eight names that
# diverge TODAY, and this file pins that no NEW symbol has started to.
# WHY AN ORACLE AND NOT AN EXPORT CHECK. "verify the symbol is exported" does NOT
# catch this class: BOTH `_fstat` and `_fstat$INODE64` exist in libSystem's
# x86_64 slice, so an export check answers YES for the WRONG one. Declaring the
# plain name there binds the LEGACY 32-bit-inode callee while DSS compiles the
# modern 144-byte `struct stat` — 120 bytes written into 144, `st_size` read at
# 96 and written at 72, `fstat` returns 0, and sqlite calls every database
# "database disk image is malformed". It links clean and loads clean. The only
# question that separates the two spellings is the one this file answers.
#   `symbol`      the C identifier a descriptor declares (keyed by NAME, not by
#                 descriptor: 41 identifiers are declared by two descriptors —
#                 math/tgmath, string/memory, unistd/sys.sysctl — and the link
#                 name is a property of the PLATFORM, so the two must agree).
#   `probeHeader` the header the measurement included. USUALLY the descriptor's
#                 own `header`, but 16 rows differ because DSS's shipped headers
#                 are a deliberate SUPERSET of the platform's: `statfs`/`fstatfs`
#                 live in DSS's <unistd.h> and in Darwin's <sys/mount.h>,
#                 `setlocale` in DSS's <stdlib.h> and Darwin's <locale.h>, and so
#                 on. Recorded per row because a probe that guesses the header
#                 reports `<compile-failed>` and would silently measure NOTHING
#                 for exactly the symbols most likely to be renamed — `statfs`
#                 and `fstatfs` are TWO OF THE EIGHT that diverge.
#   `emitted-*`   the EXACT undefined symbol `nm -u` printed, DECORATED (Mach-O's
#                 leading `_` included) because that is what the tool printed and
#                 a table of measurements must not silently edit its readings.
#                 The test strips the format's decoration itself, through the
# HOW TO REGENERATE (needs a real Mac; `dssharness host-exec --ssh macos` reaches
# the operator's). Per symbol, per arch:
# Exactly one undefined symbol comes back; that is the cell. A `<compile-failed>`
# means the probe header is wrong for THIS platform — fix `probeHeader`, never
# MEASURED 2026-08-25 on macOS 26.5.2 (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64 host), Apple `cc`
# probes, every one returning exactly one undefined symbol. EIGHT diverge:
# stat fstat lstat statfs fstatfs opendir readdir (x86_64 only, `$INODE64`) and
# realpath (BOTH arches, `$DARWIN_EXTSN`). No other identifier is renamed on
# EXTENDED 2026-08-31 (cycle P46, lane `dw`) by ELEVEN rows — <tgmath.h>'s
# complex counterparts cabs cacos casin catan ccos cexp clog cpow csin csqrt
# ctan — on macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83, Darwin 25.6.0, arm64 host), Apple clang
# 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101), MacOSX.sdk 26.5. The HOST MOVED between the two
# measurements (26.5.2 -> 26.6.2, and a newer toolchain), which is stated rather
# than smoothed over: every cell above was taken on the older one and is NOT
# re-asserted here. 66 probes for the eleven (11 x 3 candidate headers x 2
# arches); the 22 that count each returned exactly one undefined symbol.
# NONE of the eleven diverges — the emission is the plain decorated identifier
# on BOTH arches, so all eleven imply an ABSENT `linkName`, which is the arm a
# one-sided table would get wrong in the flattering direction.
# ⚠ THE PROBE HEADER WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, and the guess was WRONG: the
# brief expected these to need <complex.h> the way statfs needs <sys/mount.h>.
# `tgmath.h` — the descriptor's OWN header — compiles all eleven on both arches,
# and so does `complex.h`; `math.h` is the one that fails (`use of undeclared
# identifier 'csqrt'`). The descriptor's own header is recorded, per the
# ⓘ A SECOND measurement the oracle does not ask for was taken in the same
# session, because DSS EAGER-IMPORTS every function a descriptor lists and one
# ABSENT symbol breaks the LOAD of every binary including the header: all eleven
# LINK on both arches against libSystem, and csqrt/cabs/cpow were RUN natively
# clang 18.1.3 and ucrtbase.dll produced for the same inputs in P46).
# EXTENDED 2026-10-01 (cycle P69, lane `cs`) by TWO rows -- nan and nanf, the
# non-literal `s` (math.json's two new rows) -- on macOS (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64
# 20261001-151822-09de8866): each returned exactly one undefined symbol, the plain
# decorated identifier on BOTH arches (an ABSENT `linkName`). Because DSS
# eager-imports every function a descriptor lists, the import was also LINKED on
# both arches against libSystem and RUN natively (exit 42), run
# EXTENDED 2026-09-23 (P68 round 9, lane `lm`) by THREE rows — `getopt`,
# <unistd.h>, for `getopt`) import on Mach-O — measured on the operator's Mac
# batch of six probes (3 x 2 arches), each returning exactly one undefined
# symbol. `getopt` was probed through <unistd.h>, where Darwin declares it;
# the other two through <getopt.h>. NONE diverges: the plain decorated
# identifier on BOTH arches, so all three imply an ABSENT `linkName`.
# EXTENDED 2026-09-24 (P68 round 12, lane `lm`) by TWELVE rows — the <stdlib.h>
# functions fold S1 of D-C-STDLIB-H-LACKS-THIRTY-FIVE-ISO-NAMES imports on
# Mach-O: _Exit aligned_alloc at_quick_exit atoll div ldiv llabs lldiv mblen
# quick_exit strtof strtoull — measured on the
# operator's Mac (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64 host), Apple clang 21.0.0
# -fno-stack-protector -w -c`, `nm -u`), two batches of sixteen probes (one per
# arch), each returning exactly one undefined symbol. NONE diverges: the plain
# decorated identifier on BOTH arches, so all twelve imply an ABSENT
# `linkName`. (MB_CUR_MAX's `__mb_cur_max` is a DATUM, not a function, and so
# has no row here; the batches' four wide-character probes — mbstowcs mbtowc
# wcstombs wctomb, the same plain names — wait for S2 to import them.)
# EXTENDED 2026-10-01 (P69, lane `lm`) by TWENTY-EIGHT rows, and TEN rows LEFT.
# Measured on the operator's Mac (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64 host), Apple clang 21.0.0
# -fno-stack-protector -w -c`, `nm -u` — one probe per identifier per arch (56,
# returning exactly one undefined symbol, and NONE diverges: every cell is the
# plain decorated identifier on BOTH arches.
#   * TWELVE public imports the round's rows added: fgetpos fsetpos setbuf
#     tmpfile tmpnam (stdio.h), imaxabs imaxdiv (inttypes.h), mbstowcs mbtowc
#   * FIFTEEN PRIVATE rows — `__dss_platform_<x>`, the only way DSS's own runtime
#     inttypes.c) reach libSystem (C 7.1.3 reserves the double underscore for
#     the implementation, so no program can collide with one). A private row's
#     identifier is DSS's and its LINK NAME is the platform's; the cell is what
#     Apple cc emits for that platform identifier, which the row names in its
#     stdio.h), strtol strtoll strtoul strtoull (stdlib.h), strtoimax strtoumax
#   * `call_once` — the one row whose identifier Apple's SDK does not declare at
#     all (no <threads.h> on macOS: ✔MEASURED, `'threads.h' file not found` on
#     both arches, run 20261001-022915-5ebff155). DSS binds C's call_once on
#     Mach-O to libSystem's `pthread_once` (`linkName`), the function with C's
#     contract there, so the cell is what Apple cc emits for `&pthread_once`
#     through <pthread.h>: `_pthread_once` on both arches, implying linkName
# LEFT: fprintf printf snprintf sprintf sscanf strtol strtoll strtoul strtoull
# vfprintf — on Mach-O each is DSS's C23 entry point now (`__dss_isoc23_<name>`,
# realized from DSS's runtime source), not an import, so the census no longer
# names them (axis 3: no row outlives its symbol). Their 2026-08-25 readings
# were the plain names; the platform functions they named are imported through
# the private rows above, re-measured here.
# EXTENDED 2026-10-07 (P69, lane `cs`) by SEVEN rows -- the ISO C functions
# string.json and ctype.json now import on Mach-O too: strcoll strxfrm strpbrk
# strtok (C89), isblank (C99, through <ctype.h>), memccpy and strndup (C23) --
# measured on the operator's Mac (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64 host), Apple clang
# macos-arm64-release by THIS file's method (`#include <HEADER>` and
# -fno-stack-protector -w -c`, `nm -u`), one probe per identifier per arch (14,
# returning exactly one undefined symbol. NONE diverges: the plain decorated
# identifier on BOTH arches, so all seven imply an ABSENT `linkName`. Because
# DSS eager-imports every function a descriptor lists, the seven were also
# LINKED on x86_64 (`nm -u` of the image names all seven) and RUN natively on
# arm64 (exit 42), and libSystem's `dlsym` finds each, in the same run.
